chapter: On the road and into brass bands
title: Going on the road and playing with Smiley Lewis
summary: Touring began in the mid-1950s with Smiley Lewis, a harmonica player and Papa Lightfoot.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So how often did you go out on the road? I mean, was this for how many years?

I actually didn't start going on the road until the very late, late 50s, middle 50s, 55. That's when it really started going on the road for me. Otherwise it was like, I call it going on the road when we started going to places like Meridian, Mississippi, Club Alley, Michigan, Alabama, and Birmingham, and stuff like that. Anything over 200, 300 miles from home than we were on the road. Mm-hmm. But I mean, going up to Vashery and places on the River Road, it's just local. Yeah. We played a lot of that. When we started going on the road, that's what we were doing. We were playing Lil Rock and so forth. In those days, from Professor Longhand, I started playing with Smiley Lewis.
Yeah. Played with Smiley for a long time.

Smiley was a hell of a blues singer, man. And I forget all the people that really we played with Smiley. It was older musicians. I just can't remember. I remember Senegal played with Smiley with us for a while. He had a drummer. It looked like it was double Johnny. Boy, he was a strong little fella. And I can't remember his name. But we had good times with Smiley. We played with Smiley. And then a little guy came out of Mississippi. From Natchez. His name was Luke. We called him Jupe. Jupe. He played harmonica. Man. I can't remember his name anyhow. But we went on the road together. And we started going to places like Nashville, Tennessee, to play clubs in Nashville. And around the surrounding areas of Georgia. And so forth. With Smiley Lewis. And Papa Lightfoot.
